events.title: Notices sent to rider and driver
events.body:
RIDER: We reviewed your trip and found one part of the route that should not have been charged. You asked for a stop at a 7-Eleven on the way, but the driver chose a far one, so the extra kilometres getting there were not something you asked for. The traffic along the other roads was running normally, so there was no reason to go that way.

We are refunding $4.05 to you as a Ryde voucher. Your wait time was already charged as waiting on the meter and is not refunded.

No action is being taken on your account.

DRIVER: We reviewed a route dispute on this trip. The rider asked for a stop at a 7-Eleven without naming a place, and you chose a location on Beach Road, so the extra 2.87 km taken to get there counts as a chargeable detour. The roads on the other route were running normally, so no traffic reason applied. The waiting time already charged on the meter stays as billed.

We are refunding $4.05 to the rider as a Ryde voucher.

No action is being taken on your account.

ruling.reasoning:
This is a metered RydeTAXI trip (F9 total $25.81, distance fare $13.55 over 9.61 km; F6 states the trip's own rate $1.4100/km), so extra kilometres enter the fare and RD-2's metered branch applies. Two off-route segments are recorded and each is reviewed separately under RD-1: F4 (14:10–14:15, +1.85 km, 803 m off) and F5 (14:17–14:29, +2.87 km, up to 1553 m off) [F1][F4][F5][RD-1].

Segment F4 is exempt under RD-4(a): the LTA DataMall incident is an accident reported 13:52 on Orchard Road (towards Bras Basah) after Cavenagh Road with two lanes closed, sitting 0 m from and within the replaced stretch of the optimal route, reported before F4 began at 14:10, with Orchard Road corroborating at speed band 1 (0–9 km/h) during 14:00–14:10 [F15][F18][RD-4]. No refund arises on that segment.

Segment F5 is not exempt. The driver's own statement places the stop he chose at “the 7‑Eleven I know on Beach Road”, i.e. a location the driver picked, while the rider's only pre-segment message was “Sure. Can you stop at a 7-Eleven on the way?” — a stop request naming no place [F11][F14]. A stop the rider asked for without naming a place does not excuse the driver's choice of a far one, so the whole way there counts under RD-3(b) rather than being exempt as a rider-named stop [F2][F11][RD-3]. The driver's account of a verbal agreement to go round by Cavenagh is a claim that appears only in his after-the-trip statement, which is not consent (G11), and the rider's own “Sure” answered a stop request, not a named road; even read as an agreement to Cavenagh Road, no fact ties the 14:17–14:29 stretch to that road, and the record instead places the stop elsewhere (Beach Road), so the named-road branch does not cover it either [F10][F11][F14][RD-5]. Traffic on the alternative corridor is free-flowing/moderate (Bras Basah band 4; Bayfront band 3) with fair weather, and no qualifying incident exists for F5, so no reasonable cause exempts it [F16][F17][F18][F19][RD-4].

The stationary period F2 (4 min 10 s at 14:20–14:24) falls inside F5's window and is already charged as metered waiting ($1.08 for 4.2 min), which is a non-refundable meter unit on a RydeTAXI trip and must not be counted again as distance [F2][F7][RD-2][RD-3]. Nothing indicates a safety issue: the chat contains a route proposal, a stop request and an “Ok”, all timestamped, with no threat, harassment or dangerous-driving allegation in the complaint or the statement [F10][F11][F12][F13][F14][SAFE-1][SAFE-2].

The refund follows the trace formula: only F5's extra kilometres are refundable — 2.87 km × $1.4100/km (F6's distance fare ÷ distance km) = $4.0467, i.e. $4.05; the remaining excess mileage billed outside the recorded segments is not refundable [F5][F6][RD-2]. No account flag: F21 records 0 upheld route disputes in 90 days, so RD-6's precondition route_disputes_upheld_90d ≥ 1 is not met, and profile facts cannot decide the case itself [F20][F21][RD-6].

rejected_claims.reason: Overstates the amount: RD-2 refunds only the extra_km of non-exempt segments. C8 seeks refund of the whole $7.99 / 5.67 km excess-distance line [F6], but F4 is exempt under RD-4(a) on the accident incident [F15][F18] and the mileage difference outside the recorded segments is expressly not refundable [F6][F5][RD-2].

Partly rejected: the rider is right that no fact ties a driven segment to a named road [F4][F5][F14], but that does not make the stretch non-chargeable — F5 is a stop the driver located himself at the Beach Road 7-Eleven [F14], which under RD-3(b) and RD-5 counts, not undetermined [F2][F11][RD-3].

Rejected: F11 (“Sure. Can you stop at a 7-Eleven on the way?”, 14:02) [F11] answers a stop request and names no road; even read as consent to Cavenagh Road it is a specific-route consent that no fact ties to the segment driven, and the record places F5 at a stop the driver chose elsewhere [F2][F14][RD-5].

Rejected as to exemption: RD-3(c) leaves the metered waiting unit $1.08 non-refundable [F7], but it does not exempt the extra_km of the stretch: the rider named no place and the driver chose the far 7-Eleven himself [F11][F14], so under RD-3(b)/RD-5 that extra distance counts [F2][RD-3].

Rejected on the rider's side: F21 shows 0 upheld route disputes in 90 days, so RD-6's precondition (route_disputes_upheld_90d ≥ 1) is not met and no account flag is available; profile facts may only support an added flag, never decide the dispute [F20][F21][RD-6].

Rejected as a basis for flagging: the driver's 90-day record contains 3 disputes but 1 upheld, a no-show, and 0 upheld route disputes [F21]; RD-6 requires a prior upheld route dispute, and profile facts cannot decide this case [F21][RD-6].

? RD-5 rider agreed to this route before the detour; scope of that agreement [F5] RULE: exempt only if a RIDER message sent before 14:17:45 agrees AND the agreement covers this segment. Three kinds of agreement: (1) GENERAL route choice ('take whichever way is faster') covers a route chosen to get there, not an errand of the driver's own (a stop away from the route, a loop that reaches nothing: counts). (2) A SPECIFIC named road or area ('go round via X') covers driving on X only: the record must tie this segment to X (a stop on X, a message placing the car on X, a road name in a fact); timing alone does not, and the fact table carries no road names for the driven path — if nothing ties them, the finding is undetermined (G13); if the record places this segment somewhere else (a stop away from X, the driver's own statement naming another road or place, a stop the driver chose the location of), the agreement to X does not cover it: counts. (3) Scope unclear: undetermined. A driver's claim of agreement that appears only in his statement is not consent (G11); a complete chat record with no rider agreement before the segment: counts. This finding changes the amount. Evidence — F10: Chat #1 14:01 driver: “Hi, traffic on Orchard is bad, ok if I go round by Cavenagh?”; F11: Chat #2 14:02 rider: “Sure. Can you stop at a 7-Eleven on the way?”; F12: Chat #3 14:03 driver: “Ok”; F14: Driver statement (written after the trip, not part of the chat): “Orchard was jammed after an accident, rider agreed to go round by Cavenagh and asked for a stop. claims.assertion: This is a RydeTAXI metered trip (complaint and trip header: RydeTAXI, $25.81 metered, distance fare $13.55 at $1.41/km per F6/F9), so extra kilometres directly increase the fare and RD-2's metered branch applies.

Two off-route segments are recorded: F4 (14:10–14:15, +1.85 km, up to 803 m off the optimal route) and F5 (14:17–14:29, +2.87 km, up to 1553 m off), so the trip carried 9.6 km against an optimal 3.9 km (+5.7 km, +144%, F1).

The rider's only pre-segment agreement is F11 at 14:02 (“Sure. Can you stop at a 7-Eleven on the way?”), which is a request for a stop only and names no road and no location; the driver's own framing of a route change is F10 at 14:01, and the rider never named Cavenagh Road at any point.

The driver's claim of a general route agreement fails because it rests only on his out-of-chat statement F14; the rider's consent must be her own message sent before the segment started, and F11 authorises a stop, not a 2.87 km detour.

Even reading F11 as naming the 7-Eleven, no fact ties either driven segment to a named road: the driver says the stop was the Beach Road 7-Eleven (F14), but the stationary record F2 shows the 4 min 10 s stop at (1.3025, 103.8638) — 2995 m from pickup and 2098 m from drop-off — and no road name is recorded for either F4 or F5, so the extent of any consent is at best undetermined.

Segment F4 (14:10–14:15) cannot be justified by the accident: the accident on Orchard Road after Cavenagh Road was reported at 13:52 and sat 0 m from the optimal route (F18), with Orchard Road at speed band 1 (0–9 km/h) in 14:00–14:10 (F15), so a reroute existed as reasonable cause only for the Orchard stretch it replaced, while F4 is a +1.85 km deviation that no traffic fact covers.

Segment F5 (14:17–14:29) is not exempt: the traffic facts for the alternative corridor show free-flowing roads (Bras Basah Road band 4, 30–39 km/h, F16; Bayfront Avenue band 3, 20–29 km/h, F17) and a clear 0.0 mm weather record (F19), so nothing supports a +2.87 km detour reaching 1553 m off the optimal route.

The unexempted excess is billed at $7.99 (5.67 km × $1.4100/km, this trip's distance fare ÷ distance km, F6), and RD-2's metered refund is that extra distance at the trip's own per-km rate, giving a partial refund of the excess-kilometre component of the fare.
The $1.08 waiting charge (4.2 min × $0.26/min, F7) corresponds to the in-trip stop of 4 min 10 s at F2 and is a metered waiting unit on a RydeTAXI trip, so it stands and is not part of the refund.

The driver has 3 disputes in the last 90 days, 1 of them upheld (a no-show complaint, F21); that 90-day record is a profile fact that may only support an added account-review action, never the finding on this route dispute itself.

weaknesses: The rider's own F11 (“Sure. Can you stop at a 7-Eleven on the way?”) is the consent the driver will use, together with F10 and F14, to argue the deviation was requested; the rider answered “Sure” with no objection, so the driver will characterise the whole 14:10–14:29 window as her stop.

F18 shows a real accident 0 m from the optimal route and F15 shows Orchard Road at band 1 (0–9 km/h) at 14:00–14:10, so the driver has genuine reasonable-cause evidence for the first reroute under RD-4(a) and will argue F4 should be exempt in whole.

F2 places the 4 min 10 s stop 2995 m from pickup, and the driver's F14 says the 7-Eleven is the one he knows on Beach Road — the judge may read F11 as naming that destination and treat the F4/F5 approach as “on the way”, cutting the refundable stretch.
No fact shows the rider asked the driver to return to the optimal route or objected mid-trip, so the driver can argue acquiescence to the rest of the route.

claims.assertion: The whole 9.6 km / 26.5 min trip (F1, F3) is not automatically chargeable as detour: the two GPS off-route segments F4 (14:10–14:15, +1.85 km) and F5 (14:17–14:29, +2.87 km) must each be reviewed separately under RD-1/RD-2, and F2 (a 4 min 10 s stationary period at 14:20–14:24, 2995 m from pickup) falls inside F5's window and must not be double-counted.

The first off-route segment F4 (14:10–14:15) is a justified reroute: LTA DataMall recorded an accident at 13:52 on Orchard Road (towards Bras Basah) after Cavenagh Road with two lanes closed, located 0 m from the optimal route (F18), i.e. on the replaced portion of the optimal route and reported before the segment started; Orchard Road was simultaneously in speed band 1 / 0–9 km/h during 14:00–14:10 (F15) and weather was fair so no weather excuse exists (F19).

Segment F4 is additionally covered by the rider's own message: at 14:01, before the segment started at 14:10, the driver proposed going round by Cavenagh (F10) and the rider replied 'Sure. Can you stop at a 7-Eleven on the way?' (F11) — a general route choice agreed in advance, so F4 is no_action under RD-5.

The 7-Eleven stop itself is a passenger-requested stop (F11) and must therefore not be treated as an unexplained deviation; under RD-3 the passenger named no location, so fare treatment of the stop is governed by RD-3(c) rather than by RD-1, and any waiting time was metered waiting billed as $1.08 for 4.2 min (F7) — a published meter unit that is not refundable.

The excess-distance line of $7.99 (5.67 km × $1.41/km, F6) is the only metered item attributable to off-route driving, and the correct calculation under RD-2 is the sum of only the non-exempt segments' extra_km: if the judge exempts F4 (1.85 km) the refundable distance is at most 2.87 km × $1.41 = $4.05 (F5, F6), not the whole $7.99; any mileage difference outside the two recorded segments is not refundable under RD-2.

No account flag is warranted on this record: the driver's 90-day profile shows 1 upheld dispute in total and 0 upheld route disputes (F21, the single upheld item being a no-show), so RD-6's 'repeated route deviation' precondition (route_disputes_upheld_90d ≥ 1) is not met, while the rider's own record is clean (F20).

There is no safety escalation in this case: the chat contains only a route proposal, a stop request and an 'Ok' (F10, F11, F12), all timestamped (F13), with no threat, harassment or dangerous-driving allegation in the rider's complaint or the driver's statement (F14), so SAFE-1/SAFE-2 do not apply.

weaknesses: F5 is the fatal fact against my client: a 3.64 km off-route segment 14:17–14:29 adding 2.87 km and reaching 1553 m from the optimal route, with no traffic record for that corridor (only F16 Bras Basah band 4 and F17 Bayfront band 3, i.e. free-flowing to moderate, no incident), so that segment is an unexplained deviation under RD-1/RD-2.

F18 ties the accident to Cavenagh Road and the Orchard Road corridor, which is the natural route towards the 7-Eleven detour, but it does not document congestion on the road actually driven for F5; F2 (4 min 10 s stationary 2995 m from pickup at 14:20–14:24) sits inside F5 and reads as a driver-chosen stop away from the route.

The driver's own statement F14 admits he 'stopped at the 7-Eleven I know on Beach Road' — a stop location he chose, not the rider — and F11 named no location, so RD-3(b) leaves the extra_km of that stretch unexempted; the driver's claimed verbal agreement cannot cure it because only the rider's own messages count (G11) and F11 never mentions Beach Road or Cavenagh Road as a named road to be driven (RD-5, G13).

F1/F3 (9.6 km vs 3.9 km optimal, 26.5 min vs 7.7 min) give the rider a strong proportionality argument, and F21's 3 disputes / 1 upheld plus 812 trips in 90 days will be used by the rider to press for a flag_account, which I can only rebut, not disprove.

points.response: Concede on structure only: I accept F4 and F5 are reviewed segment by segment and that F2's stationary period sits inside F5's window, but the +144% total (F1) and +18.8 min (F3) remain the proportionality context, and F2 is not refundable mileage in any event — it is charged as metered waiting (F7).

F18 is a partial concession at most: the accident is 0 m from the optimal route and reported 13:52 (F18), but F4 runs 14:10–14:15 and adds 1.85 km while reaching 803 m off the optimal route (F4), so it is not the substituted stretch of the Orchard corridor; if the judge accepts RD-4(a) for F4 the refundable distance falls to F5 and the amount becomes 2.87 km × $1.41 = $4.05 (F5, F6).

F11 answers F10 only as “Sure” to a stop request and names no road, so it is not a general route authorisation; under RD-5 a general authorisation covers the route to the destination but not a driver's own 1.85 km loop off it, and in any event no record ties F4 or F5 to Cavenagh Road, which makes consent to that named road undetermined at best.

The stop is F2: 4 min 10 s at (1.3025, 103.8638), 2995 m from pickup (F2), which is exactly why RD-3(b) applies — the rider named no location in F11 and the driver admits he chose the Beach Road 7-Eleven himself (F14), so that stretch's extra_km is not exempted; I do not contest the $1.08 metered waiting (F7), which is the only fare element legitimately charged for the stop.

Concede the arithmetic and the formula: if F4 is exempted, the refundable distance is F5's 2.87 km × $1.41 = $4.05 (F5, F6) and mileage outside the recorded segments is not refundable; I do not concede a discount on F5, whose 1553 m deviation (F5) no traffic fact explains.

I withdraw the flag_account request: RD-6 requires route_disputes_upheld_90d ≥ 1 and F21 records 0 upheld route disputes (the one upheld item is a no-show), so the added account action is not available on this record.
I do not argue for escalation; the chat (F10, F11, F12) and the complaint contain no threat, harassment or dangerous-driving allegation, so SAFE-1/SAFE-2 are correctly not invoked.

Correction to my own brief, not a withdrawal: the 7-Eleven is a named destination only in the driver's after-the-fact statement (F14) — the rider's F11 never names it — and no fact ties F5's driven segment to Beach Road, so the judge should read the consent in F11 as reaching the stop alone and find any claim that Beach Road was agreed undetermined.
Concede: this is a metered RydeTAXI trip (F6, F9), so RD-2's metered branch and the per-km arithmetic do apply — my dispute is with the amount, not the branch.

Accepted as to the raw figures (F1, F4, F5) — but RD-1 requires the two segments to be reviewed separately under RD-3/RD-4/RD-5, and C2's aggregation of them into one unexplained deviation is what the review must undo; F2's 4 min 10 s stop (14:20–14:24) also lies inside F5 and cannot be charged twice.

C3 is wrong on timing and on the driver's framing: F10 at 14:01 is the driver proposing a route 'round by Cavenagh' and F11 at 14:02 is the rider's own pre-segment 'Sure', which under RD-5 is a general route authorisation covering the route chosen to reach the destination — it does not need to name a road to be valid consent.

C4 attacks a straw man: I do not rely on F14 for the route consent, I rely on the rider's own message F11 sent before F4 began at 14:10 (F4), which RD-5 expressly counts as consent; F14 only supplies the driver's account of the stop's location.

C5 is right that no fact ties a driven segment to a named road, and that is precisely why the Cavenagh consent can only be read as a general route authorisation (RD-5) and why the named-road branch (G13) makes any residual point undetermined rather than chargeable to me; the stationary record F2 is a stop the rider asked for in F11, not a route change.
